slides.scene: Four guests who all quarrel sit on a 4 × 4 floor of cushions. Any two in the same row, column or diagonal start a fight. Seat all four in peace.

blocks.text: These two share a diagonal: a fight. In how many ways can all four sit in peace?

slides.title: LeetCode 51
slides.lead: Place n queens on an n × n board so no two attack. Return every board.

blocks.text: n is 1 to 9. A queen attacks along its row, column and both diagonals.

slides.try_first: Place 4 queens on a 4 × 4 grid you draw. Where must the queen in row 0 go?

slides.title: Try every board
slides.lead: Choose any 4 of the 16 squares, then check if two queens attack.

blocks.text: Billions of boards by n = 8. Most of them are hopeless from the second queen.

slides.title: One queen per row
slides.lead: Two queens in a row attack, so each row holds exactly one. Only its column is a choice.

quickcheck.question: Queens at row 0 col 0 and row 1 col 2. Which columns of row 2 are safe?
quickcheck.answer: Answer: {{safe_cols([0, 2], 2, 4)}}. Columns 0 and 2 are taken, 1 and 3 are on a diagonal.

slides.title: Back up and move
slides.lead: Backtracking from post 38: place row by row. No safe column? The queen above moves.

blocks.text: Like seating guests who quarrel: seat them row by row, and when nobody fits, reseat the last guest.

slides.title: The safe test
slides.lead: Keep queens[r] = the column of the queen in row r. A new square (row, col) is attacked by row r when:

blocks.text: col == c   or   col == c ± (row − r)
c = queens[r]. The first is the same column; the second, the same diagonal.
Rows below are empty, so only rows above need checking.

slides.lead: Box r holds the column of row r's queen.

slides.title: Is it safe?
slides.lead: Check the new square against the queen in every row above.

blog.summary: Place n queens so none attack: one per row, a safe test against the rows above, and back up when a row has no safe column.
blog.tested_what: The row-by-row search and the safe test
blog.tested_inputs: every n from 1 to 9 (all boards compared, 352 of them for n = 9), and the safe test on hand-picked squares and random partial boards of up to 9 columns
blog.tested_against: a brute force that tries every order of columns and checks every pair of queens
blog.tested_extra: The placements and back-ups in the walk-through and the quick-check answer come from running the code.

caption.first: LeetCode 51 N-Queens solved with backtracking: one queen per row, a safe test, and back up when a row has no safe column.
lines: Two queens in a row attack, so each row holds one queen and only its column is a choice.
A square is attacked by row r's queen at column c when col == c or col == c ± (row − r).
